edit.description: the inbox window's lane leg, beside the record and refusal legs
the reader reports the run's identity and whether it failed, for the leg to compare against the stamp
the slice stamps the run it drained, as it stamps a cursor
the lane leg over the stub forge CLI: red past the stamp, red already stamped, green, unreadable

summary: a declared lane never wakes the inbox slice, so a quiet tree hibernates over a red lane — and with no closing condition a woken lane would re-drain the same run every tick

per.section: CI lanes as a findings source

acceptance: the inbox slice is live for a declared lane exactly when that lane's latest completed run for the tip's branch failed and is past the lane's stamp; a green run, an already-stamped run, and a lane it cannot read each make it live for nothing.
tests: the inbox slice is live when a declared lane's latest completed run failed past the lane's stamp
the inbox slice is not live when the lane's failing run is the one already stamped
the inbox slice is not live when the lane's latest completed run passed
the inbox slice is not live when the forge CLI cannot read the lane
notes: `PlanSliceWindow.live` is sync and runs on the selection path (planState.ts), so the lane read has a sync half — once per tick per lane, beside the render's. `SliceInputs` carries no working tree, so the liveness leg must read the branch at the same repo root the render does (`ci.ts`, *The branch is the repo's*) or the two readers name different runs. The agent writes the stamp as it writes a cursor, so the rendered block must name the run it would stamp.

edit.description: the silent arm takes absence from the path, not from an errno that means two things
the obstructed-root case, asserted on the refusal rather than on a platform's errno

summary: readAll reads `ENOENT` from the keyspace readdir as nothing-written, and on win32 a plain file at the prior-attempts root raises exactly that — an unreachable store reports as no records
acceptance: an obstructed prior-attempts root refuses on every supported host, and only a genuinely absent path reads as no records.
pins: readAll refuses when a plain file sits at the prior-attempts root
notes: Lane-observed: `readAll refuses when the prior-attempts dir is present but unreadable` resolved `Map{}` on windows-latest where POSIX raises ENOTDIR. The doc comment on readAll already names this exact degradation as the one it refuses to make. No `tests[]`: the errno split is unreproducible on a POSIX base, so the windows lane's own title is the verification (`spec/cli.md`, *win32 is a supported host*). Sibling ENOENT-means-absent arms in src/job.ts are not yet lane-evidenced.
